source.title: Depthwise Separable Convolutions Allow for Fast and Memory-Efficient Spectral Normalization
source.authors: Christina Runkel; C. Etmann; Michael Möller; C. Schönlieb

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices and experimental tables.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports training outcomes for spectrally normalized networks, but does not measure training classification error or test the claim versions about reaching near-zero error, bad minima, depth, initialization, learning-rate stability, or batch normalization speed.
record.gate_note: Training accuracies for the claim's target behavior are not reported. Table 1 reports CIFAR-10 test accuracy under spectral normalization and varying learning rates/scaling constants, not training classification error. ImageNet reports validation accuracy. Timing results compare spectral normalization overhead, not convergence to low training error. These do not qualify as rows under the stated extraction rules.
record.test_reason: The study benchmarks spectral normalization accuracy, classification generalization, and computational overhead. It does not test any claim version: training classification error is unreported; initialization observations concern a spectral-scaling parameter rather than activation-matched initialization in plain networks; learning-rate experiments do not measure stability thresholds or curvature; and no batch-normalization comparison is made.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors propose fast, memory-efficient spectral normalization for depthwise separable convolutions, with accurate bounds in practice for unit-stride layers and approximately 2% epoch-time overhead on ImageNet. Their experiments also show substantially looser bounds for strided layers and approximately 63% overhead on CIFAR-10.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies efficient spectral normalization of depthwise separable convolutions; its classification experiments do not evaluate the claim's training-error outcomes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test and validation accuracy varies with the scaling constant and learning rate; the paper says high learning rates may collapse training, and ImageNet soft-scaling initialization required adjustment at higher scaling constants.

fits_no_version.finding: CIFAR-10 test accuracy depends on the spectral scaling constant and learning rate; the authors report that excessive learning rates can collapse training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning rates require tuning to the strength of spectral constraints in these depthwise separable networks.

fits_no_version.finding: For ImageNet with soft scaling and K above 20, initializing s at 3 caused exploding gradients or missing convergence; reducing it to 0.5 enabled training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Initialization of the learnable spectral-scaling parameter affects convergence in spectrally normalized MobileNetV2.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral normalization increased epoch time by factors of 1.63 on CIFAR-10 and 1.02 on ImageNet.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The computational overhead of this spectral-normalization procedure depends on the architecture and workload.

record.problems: The paper reports test or validation accuracy rather than training classification error for its benchmark experiments. Accuracy results in Figure 3 are figure-only in the supplied text; no training-error measurements are given.
record.rows_left_out: No rows meet the required outcome measure: Table 1 reports test accuracy, Figure 3 reports ImageNet validation accuracy, and Table 2 reports epoch time. These are not measurements of the claim's training-error behavior.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error, including random or corrupted labels, and its dependence on model size or training recipe.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems and their dependence on student width.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and the specified alternative initialization recipes.
Activation-matched initialization, signal and gradient propagation across depth, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and trainable depth in plain networks.
Recovery above the initial stability limit, loss and curvature trajectories, edge-of-stability behavior, and divergence relative to measured thresholds.
Batch normalization versus no normalization in convergence speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation='tests' conflicts with its otherwise appropriate T6 assessment. Keeping rows empty is appropriate. Training without batch normalization alone does not test V6, and the scaling-parameter initialization observation does not test V4.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, corrupted or random labels, model size, and effects of early stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual depth effects on training error, and the cited special-initialization or normalization-free residual results.
Initialization comparisons and their effects on training speed or trainable depth.
Training dynamics above a stability limit, sharpness behavior, and divergence relative to stability thresholds.
Batch normalization effects on training speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup performance without normalization.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
